```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages(library(readxl))
P    <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/GLI-Hedgehog_Signaling"
GS   <- file.path(P, "data/gene_sets")
sf   <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "SFARI_cat1_cat2_07-12-2026release.tsv"))
tada <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "TADA_Fu2022_per_gene.tsv"))
ndd  <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "NDD_genes.tsv"))
gs   <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "enrichment_gene_sets.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
cl   <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_clusters/maSigPro_clusters_hgnc.tsv"))
load(file.path(GS, "Gene_Set_List_UPDATED_sfarionly12_tadaupdated_sczdd.rdata"))  # advisor's lists
adv  <- Gene_Set_List
fmt  <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
```

Three sources, all downloaded 11/17/2026. Raw files and the scripts that
build each list are in `r P`.

# SFARI Gene (autism)

[SFARI Gene](https://gene.sfari.org/) Human Gene Module, **release 07-12-2026**
(Q2 2026). Category 1 = high confidence, category 2 = strong candidate.

```{r sfari}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  category = c("1", "2", "1 & 2"),
  genes = c(sum(sf$gene_score == 1), sum(sf$gene_score == 2), nrow(sf)),
  syndromic = c(sum(sf$gene_score == 1 & sf$syndromic == 1),
                sum(sf$gene_score == 2 & sf$syndromic == 1), sum(sf$syndromic == 1))),
  col.names = c("SFARI category", "Genes", "Of which syndromic"))
old <- adv$SFARI_gene
```

The SFARI list in the advisor's gene-set file (`r length(old)` genes) is an
**older release** of the same categories, not a filtered one.
`r sum(old %in% sf$gene_symbol)` of its genes are still category 1–2. The
current release adds `r length(setdiff(sf$gene_symbol, old))` genes, including
CHD8, SHANK3, SYNGAP1, ARID1B and ADNP. Not included: genes listed only as
"syndromic" with no score, and category 3.

# TADA (autism): Fu et al. 2022

[Fu et al. 2022, *Nat Genet*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-022-01104-0),
Supplementary Table 11. It is the largest and most recent autism TADA analysis:
63,237 individuals, with de novo, inherited and case-control variants and CNVs.
TADA gives every gene a false discovery rate; we split them into tiers using
the paper's own thresholds.

```{r tada}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  tier = c("high", "med", "low (not used)"),
  rule = c("FDR &le; 0.001", "0.001 < FDR &le; 0.05", "0.05 < FDR &le; 0.1"),
  genes = as.vector(table(factor(tada$ASD_tier, c("high", "med", "low"))))),
  col.names = c("Tier", "Autism TADA FDR", "Genes"), escape = FALSE)
```

**Why not the advisor's `High` list?** The advisor's file has a 120-gene
TADA "High" list but no matching "Med" list, and the source of `High` is
unknown. It does not match any published TADA list we checked. Fu 2022 is the
closest:

```{r high_trace}
H <- adv$High
fu_in <- function(i) sum(H %in% c(tada$gene[i], tada$gene_gencodeV33[i]))
he <- as.data.frame(suppressMessages(read_excel(file.path(GS, "tada_he2013_raw/He2013_PLoSGenet_TableS3.xlsx"))))
sa <- as.data.frame(suppressMessages(read_excel(file.path(GS, "sanders2015_raw/Sanders2015_Neuron_TADA_Scores_mmc7.xlsx"))))
sa_q <- as.numeric(sa$tadaFdrAscSscExomeSscAgpSmallDel)
sa_in <- function(i) sum(H %in% c(sa$RefSeqGeneName[i], sa$TadaGeneName[i]))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  study = c("He et al. 2013 (PLoS Genet)", "Sanders et al. 2015 (Neuron)",
            "Fu et al. 2022, FDR &le; 0.001", "Fu et al. 2022, FDR &le; 0.05"),
  list = c(sum(he$q.TADA < 0.2), sum(sa_q <= 0.1), sum(tada$FDR_TADA_ASD <= 0.001), sum(tada$FDR_TADA_ASD <= 0.05)),
  shared = c(sum(H %in% he$Gene[he$q.TADA < 0.2]), sa_in(which(sa_q <= 0.1)),
             fu_in(tada$FDR_TADA_ASD <= 0.001), fu_in(tada$FDR_TADA_ASD <= 0.05)),
  threshold = c("q < 0.2", "q &le; 0.1", "", "")),
  col.names = c("Published TADA list", "Genes in list", "Shared with advisor's High (120)", "Threshold"),
  escape = FALSE)
```

Liu et al. 2018 (*AJHG*, TADA-A) took its TADA lists from Sanders 2015.
Its gene-set definitions match the structure of the advisor's file.

# NDD genes: Wang et al. 2022

[Wang et al. 2022, *PNAS*](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2203491119),
Dataset S6. This updates [Coe et al. 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6309590/)
(Eichler lab) with **46,612 parent–child trios**: 15,560 autism and 31,052
developmental delay.

**How the genes were found.** Only de novo mutations are used: mutations
present in the child but in neither parent. For each gene, the observed count of
damaging de novo mutations is compared with the number expected from the gene's
mutation rate. Three statistical models are used (chimpanzee–human divergence,
denovolyzeR, DeNovoWEST).

```{r ndd}
w <- ndd[ndd$source == "Wang2022", ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  tier = c("high (HC138)", "medium (MC237, not HC)", "low (LC615 only)", "all (used here)"),
  rule = c("exome-wide significant (P < 3.64e-7) in all three models",
           "FDR < 5% in all three models",
           "FDR < 5% in at least one model", ""),
  genes = c(as.vector(table(factor(w$tier, c("high", "med", "low")))), nrow(w))),
  col.names = c("Tier", "Rule", "Genes"))
coe <- ndd$gene[ndd$source == "Coe2019"]
```

Two-thirds of the trios are developmental delay, so this list leans toward DD
genes; the paper found no autism-specific genes. Of Coe 2019's
`r length(coe)` genes, `r sum(coe %in% w$gene)` are in Wang's 615.

# How much the gene sets overlap

After restricting to protein-coding genes. The diagonal is the size of each set.

```{r overlap}
sets <- c("TADA-high_fu2022", "TADA-med_fu2022", "NDD_wang2022", "SFARI_cat1", "SFARI_cat2")
L <- lapply(setNames(sets, sets), function(s) gs$hgnc_id[gs$gene_set == s])
M <- outer(sets, sets, Vectorize(function(a, b) length(intersect(L[[a]], L[[b]]))))
dimnames(M) <- list(sets, sets)
knitr::kable(M)
```

TADA and SFARI overlap heavily:
`r sum(L[["TADA-high_fu2022"]] %in% c(L[["SFARI_cat1"]], L[["SFARI_cat2"]]))` of
`r length(L[["TADA-high_fu2022"]])` TADA-high genes are SFARI category 1 or 2.
Results for different gene sets therefore partly reflect the same genes.

# Gene name harmonization

All lists and clusters were mapped to current HGNC gene IDs. Gene sets were
mapped by Ensembl or HGNC ID where available; clusters, which have symbols
only, by approved, then previous, then alias symbol.

```{r mapping}
m <- table(factor(cl$match, c("approved", "prev", "alias", "unmapped")), cl$kept)
knitr::kable(data.frame(match = rownames(m), kept = m[, "TRUE"], dropped = m[, "FALSE"]),
             col.names = c("Cluster gene matched by", "Kept (protein-coding)", "Dropped"),
             row.names = FALSE)
```
